clue.text: Film of 14 across with inch for yard — for foot

definitions.text: Film of 14 across with inch for yard
definitions.meaning: 14 across is DUSTY; swap its Y (yard) for IN (inch) to get Dustin, as in Dustin Hoffman, and this is his 1982 comedy film
a childish or playful word for a foot

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is a puzzle in itself: change the yard abbreviation Y in the 14-across answer to IN (inch), and you have the actor Dustin Hoffman, who starred in the film in drag.
explanation.definitionFit: The film starring Dustin Hoffman shares its title with a nursery word for a foot, so both senses land on one word.

clue.text: Opera heroine using three-legg'd stool when fit

indicators.note: using these words as raw material means their letters are taken and rebuilt into the title

explanation.surface: An opera heroine perches on a three-legged stool whenever she feels up to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'using' signals that every letter of THREE-LEGG'D STOOL WHEN FIT is rearranged; the apostrophe stands for a dropped E, so the count comes out exactly. The surface fit is good health, not a convulsion.
explanation.definitionFit: Puccini's opera is named after its heroine, Minnie, so its title phrase describes an opera heroine.

clue.text: See 1 down
Pole to split bill with American gladiator

parts.note: S stands for south, one of the two poles
to split is to part
AC is short for account, a bill
US means American

explanation.surface: A Pole agrees to go halves on a bill with an American gladiator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' reads as a Polish person but is just the compass pole S.
explanation.definitionFit: Spartacus was the Thracian gladiator who led the slave revolt against Rome.

clue.text: English question American horse

parts.note: US means American

explanation.surface: An English questioner asks about an American horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin word is also the title of Peter Shaffer's play about a boy who blinds horses.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Latin word for a horse, used as a genus name and as a play title.

clue.text: 40.5 gallons to be knocked down

parts.note: a pin is a small cask holding four and a half gallons, so nine of them hold 40.5 gallons
the cask in question is a pin, half a firkin

explanation.surface: A huge quantity of drink is about to be toppled over.
explanation.walkthrough: A pin is an old brewer's cask of 4.5 gallons, so nine pins make 40.5 gallons.
explanation.definitionFit: In skittles each pin is set up precisely so that it can be knocked down by the bowl.

clue.text: Name or objects for movements in the other direction

parts.note: taken as written
objects are things

explanation.surface: Someone chooses a name or some objects to describe movements going the opposite way.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'other direction' plays off 6 down, whose wordplay swaps S (south) for N (north).
explanation.definitionFit: Northings are distances travelled northward, the opposite way from southings.

clue.text: Scruff has such a reversal of direction

indicators.note: turning round from south to north means the S in these words is replaced by an N

explanation.surface: The scruff of the neck is said to turn things about in a strange way.
explanation.walkthrough: In SUCH A the S (south) is changed to N (north), the opposite direction.
explanation.definitionFit: The nucha is the anatomical name for the nape, the scruff of the neck.

clue.text: Where are the gardener's children?

parts.note: a gardener's children might be in a children's room; a gardener's young plants are raised in a place for seedlings with the same name

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a room for small children and a place where young plants are grown.

clue.text: Disentangling the Crux Australis crater — no SATS for such activities

indicators.note: untangling these words means sorting their letters into a fresh order

parts.note: Standard Assessment Tests taken in English schools, whose letters are the ones removed

explanation.surface: Someone sorting out a crater named after the Southern Cross recommends no exams for such pursuits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' takes the letters of SATS out of CRUX AUSTRALIS CRATER before the rest are rearranged; SATS are national school tests in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Activities outside the school curriculum are described by this adjective, with no exams involved.

clue.text: Foolish one — majority of planet

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: most of the word, with its last three letters dropped, is used

parts.note: Neptune is a planet

explanation.surface: A foolish person is said to own most of a planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'majority of' keeps NEPT, four of the seven letters of NEPTUNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means clumsy and lacking skill, close to foolish in behaviour.

clue.text: Coins have been used to make a sword

indicators.note: the letters have been used to build something else, which signals they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Melted-down coins have gone into forging a sword.
explanation.definitionFit: A schiavona is a basket-hilted broadsword used by the Venetian Doge's Slavonic guard.

clue.text: Late actor gave sign to compere Jerome

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac
MC means master of ceremonies, a compere
Jerome Kern was the American composer of Show Boat

explanation.surface: A late actor gave an astrological sign to a compere called Jerome.
explanation.walkthrough: Leo McKern was the Australian actor best known as Rumpole of the Bailey.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo McKern, who died in 2002, was an actor and so a late actor when this appeared.

clue.text: Strenuous discovery of truffle?

indicators.note: read as dis-covery, the letters are uncovered and laid out afresh in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Finding a truffle takes a great deal of hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovery' signals rearranging OF TRUFFLE; the question mark admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Effortful describes something requiring great exertion, which is what strenuous means.

clue.text: Not so could be an answer

definitions.meaning: the idiom 'not so ...' means not bad at all, so this word can follow 'not so'
... Answer is Rosamond Lehmann's novel, so this word can come before 'answer'

explanation.definitionFit: Both definitions are phrases completed by the word: not so ___ (not bad) and ___ Answer (the novel).

clue.text: Systematic treatment of hell and damnation cut short by the Guardian

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and so hell

indicators.note: the word loses its final letter, trimmed at the end

parts.note: a curse is a damnation
the newspaper refers to itself as us

explanation.surface: A systematic study of hell and damnation is abridged by the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' drops the E of CURSE. The Guardian setter uses US for the paper itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A discursus is a formal discourse or treatise, a systematic treatment of a subject.

clue.text: Mother and I leave Turkish boat with monkey

parts.note: ma is a word for mother

indicators.note: the letter named goes away from the word, so it is removed

parts.note: a caique is a light Turkish rowing boat

explanation.surface: Mother and I get off a Turkish boat with a monkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leave' takes the I out of CAIQUE, leaving CAQUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A macaque is a kind of Old World monkey, such as the rhesus.

clue.text: For C F# playing after isinglass is produced

indicators.note: the musical notes are being played about, their letters jumbled

parts.note: the note written F# is spoken as F sharp

explanation.surface: A piece in C and F sharp is played while isinglass is being made.
explanation.walkthrough: Spell out F# as F SHARP, then rearrange it with C and IS. Isinglass is gelatin extracted from fish bladders, and what is left after it is made is fish scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish scrap is the waste fish material remaining once isinglass has been extracted.

clue.text: Co-operate with excavation feature

parts.note: a pit is something dug out
the chin is a facial feature

explanation.surface: Someone helps out with a dig.
explanation.definitionFit: To pitch in is to join in and help, which is to co-operate.

clue.text: Riddle to study: what does Kofi have to beat?

parts.note: to con is to study or learn
Kofi Annan was Secretary-General of the UN
to drum is to beat

explanation.surface: Someone is told to study what Kofi Annan has to beat.
explanation.walkthrough: Kofi Annan headed the United Nations, the UN, when this appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: A conundrum is a puzzling question, which is what a riddle is.

clue.text: Killer of man in Japan

indicators.note: the letters come out of the run of words that follows, taken from within them

explanation.surface: A man in Japan is a killer.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through 'maN IN JApan'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ninja was a Japanese mercenary trained in covert killing and espionage.

clue.text: German flower artist loses model — put in hospital

indicators.note: the hospital letter is placed inside what remains
the named letter is dropped from the artist's name

parts.note: Claude Monet was a French artist
the Model T was Ford's famous car, so model gives T
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A German painter loses his sitter and is taken into hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' takes T from MONET; 'put in' places H inside MONE. 'Flower' means something that flows, a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Möhne is a river in Germany, famous for the dam breached in 1943; a flower is a river in crosswords.

clue.text: Needing a paper knife in original version

definitions.meaning: a book whose page edges have not been slit open needs a knife to read
a film or text not shortened or censored is in its original form

explanation.definitionFit: Unslit pages and an unabridged version are both described by the same word.

clue.text: Solomon's visitor from Dumfries

definitions.meaning: the Queen of Sheba, who visited King Solomon, is called this in the Gospels
the Scottish football club based in Dumfries has this name

explanation.definitionFit: The Bible's name for the Queen of Sheba is also the name of Dumfries's Scottish football club.

clue.text: Settlement round river for singular inside organs

indicators.note: the settlement word goes around the river letter, holding it inside

parts.note: an entail is a legal settlement of property on a line of heirs

explanation.surface: A settlement around a river is home to unique internal organs.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition asks for the singular of the usual plural for the body's insides.
explanation.definitionFit: The innards are usually called by the plural; the singular form names one internal organ.

clue.text: Great ship with energy following

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
astern means behind, following a ship

explanation.surface: A great ship has energy in her wake.
explanation.walkthrough: The Great Eastern was Brunel's huge Victorian steamship; the definition is completed by the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunel's giant steamship was called the Great Eastern, so the word follows Great to name it.
